name: Combined oral contraceptive pill

card.summary: The estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pill, also prescribed for hormonal acne in women because it lowers free androgens.
card.aka: The pill, COC, OCP; acne-approved brands include Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz and YAZ
card.note: Prescription-only; carries a small increased venous clotting risk and has formal contraindications.

quick.overview:
Combined oral contraceptives contain an estrogen and a progestin. Besides preventing pregnancy, some are prescribed to reduce acne and excess hair growth in women, because they lower the activity of androgen hormones that drive oil production in skin [1][2].

Wikipedia reports that four combined pills are FDA-approved for moderate acne in people who have started menstruating and also want contraception, and that studies show reductions in both inflammatory and non-inflammatory facial lesions [1]. Progestin-only pills have not been shown to help acne [1].
quick.mechanism: The estrogen component appears to suppress ovarian androgen production and raises sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), which reduces free testosterone. Lower free androgens mean less sebum, a major contributor to acne [1].
quick.risks: Common effects include breakthrough bleeding, nausea, headache, breast tenderness and bloating. Venous thromboembolism risk is higher in users than non-users in absolute terms (about 60 versus 30 per 100,000 woman-years) and varies by progestin; the FDA added a warning to drospirenone pill labels in 2012. Smoking over 35, migraine with aura, and a history of clots or stroke are among the listed contraindications [1].

lead: The combined oral contraceptive pill (COC) is a daily hormonal medicine containing an estrogen and a progestin, taken mainly for contraception. People use it for their appearance because it lowers androgen activity: less androgen-driven oil production can mean clearer skin, and the same effect is used to reduce unwanted facial and body hair [1][2][3].

Four combined pills are FDA-approved for moderate acne in patients at least 14 or 15 years old who have begun menstruating and also need contraception: Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz and YAZ [1]. Wikipedia reports lesion reductions of roughly 40 to 70 percent with combined pills, and a 2014 review found oral antibiotics somewhat better at three months but about equal at six months [2]. For hirsutism, Wikipedia describes combined pills as acting as functional antiandrogens, with some containing antiandrogenic progestins such as cyproterone acetate, drospirenone or dienogest [3].

In polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), where raised androgens produce acne, hirsutism and irregular cycles, the pill is one of the standard medical options alongside metformin and lifestyle changes [4][5]. It is a prescription treatment and is discussed mainly in dermatology and women's health contexts; looksmaxxing forum material specifically about it is sparse.

chain: Estrogen suppresses ovarian androgen production and raises SHBG
Less free testosterone reaches oil glands and hair follicles
Less sebum and fewer acne lesions; reduced androgen-driven hair growth
angle.text: Women with hormonal acne or androgen-related hair growth use the pill to bring free androgens down, which can lead to clearer skin and finer or less hair on the face and body. Effects build over months rather than days.

infobox: One of several standard medical options, alongside metformin

paras: Combined pills are prescribed for androgen-related acne and hirsutism [1][3]. Wikipedia reports that third- or fourth-generation progestins, or antiandrogenic ones such as cyproterone acetate, are preferred for acne, and that first-generation progestins may worsen it [2].

Hirsutism is another appearance-related use. Wikipedia reports that combined pills have supporting evidence for hirsutism and that no clear preference exists between particular pills, while antiandrogen drugs are described as the most effective pharmacologic treatment for hirsutism that bothers the patient [3].

The primary use is pregnancy prevention. In PCOS, international guidance reviewed in the 2022 Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology seminar lists the pill for menstrual-cycle regulation and androgen excess, with metformin used for insulin resistance and metabolic features [4]. Registered post-authorisation studies exist for specific products, for example a Phase 4 study of YAZ in China that enrolled 1,921 women with contraception as the condition studied [6].

Studies cited by Wikipedia show that combined pills reduce both inflammatory and non-inflammatory facial acne lesions, whereas progestin-only pills have not been shown to be effective [1]. The acne article gives a range of about 40 to 70 percent fewer lesions and describes pills as a reasonable first-line option for some women [2].

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis of 36 randomized trials in women with PCOS found no difference in hirsutism between metformin and the pill, or between the pill and the pill combined with metformin. The pill raised SHBG and lowered free androgen index and testosterone more than metformin did [5].
Breakthrough bleeding is the most common effect. Nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, fluid retention and weight change may also occur [1].

The absolute risk of venous thrombosis is reported as about 60 per 100,000 woman-years in current users versus 30 in non-users, compared with 100 to 200 per 100,000 pregnant women per year [1]. Risk varies by progestin; compared with levonorgestrel, rate ratios for deep venous thrombosis are reported as 1.82 for desogestrel, 1.86 for gestodene, 1.64 for drospirenone and 1.88 for cyproterone acetate [1]. An FDA review of more than 800,000 women led to a 2012 warning on drospirenone labels [1]. Pills with more than 50 micrograms of estrogen are linked to higher ischemic stroke and heart attack risk [1].

WHO and CDC eligibility criteria list as category 4 (should not be used) conditions such as migraine with aura, a history of DVT, pulmonary embolism or stroke, smoking 15 or more cigarettes daily at age 35 or older, blood pressure of 160/100 mm Hg or higher, known thrombogenic mutations, current breast cancer and severe cirrhosis or liver tumours. Pills should not be taken during known pregnancy [1].

For acne and hirsutism, the estrogen component appears to suppress ovarian androgen production and raise SHBG, lowering free testosterone and therefore sebum output [1]. Some progestins add direct antiandrogen activity by blocking androgen receptors [3].

The first oral contraceptive was approved by the FDA and marketed in the United States in 1960. First-generation pills used high estrogen doses; later generations lowered the estrogen and varied the progestin, with third and fourth generations arriving from the 1990s [1].

Human studies cited by reference sources report reductions in acne lesions with combined pills, and a 2014 review compared them with oral antibiotics [1][2]. A 2024 meta-analysis of 36 randomized trials compared the pill, metformin and both together in PCOS across hirsutism, hormone and metabolic outcomes [5]. A completed Phase 4 safety and efficacy study of YAZ in 1,921 Chinese women is registered, with contraception as the studied condition [6].

The pill appears in forum conversation mostly as a topic about women's hormones and partner behaviour rather than as a skin-care tool, and a minority of posts make claims about personality effects that are outside the scope of acne treatment. Hacker News has carried threads on author Sarah E. Hill's argument that the pill's influence on women's brains is under-studied [7].

timeline.event: The first oral contraceptive is approved by the FDA and marketed in the United States [1].
The FDA adds a clotting-risk warning to the drospirenone pill label [1].
A meta-analysis of 36 randomized trials compares the pill and metformin in PCOS, informing the 2023 international PCOS guideline update [5].
